_comment: Tool-enabled tasks for the codebase skill against vuln-flask (SKILLOPT_TOOLS_CWD=skill-training/fixtures/vuln-flask). Intents are NEUTRAL; every judge requires a per-finding Confidence rating (High/Medium/Low) in addition to naming the vulns + ASVS. The baseline codebase skill reliably OMITS confidence ratings, so this gap lives in the skill and appears on the held-out (val) task too — the optimizer should add a 'rate each finding's confidence' rule to the LEARNED block and the gate should accept it. See codebase-vuln-bank.json for the richer target.

tasks.intent: Perform a white-box security review of the Python Flask application in the current working directory. Read the source files (start with app.py), then produce the review INLINE as your final answer, with a section per vulnerability.
tasks.context_excerpt: A small single-file Flask service (app.py) plus a README. Review all of it.
tasks.reference: A review that finds SQL injection, OS command injection, path traversal, hardcoded secret, weak MD5 hashing, and debug mode; each finding names the vuln, its severity, an ASVS reference, and a Confidence rating (High/Medium/Low).

tasks.intent: Review the source code in the current working directory with a focus on injection flaws. Read the files, then list every injection vulnerability inline.
tasks.context_excerpt: Focus on injection: SQL, OS command, and path/file. The app is app.py.
tasks.reference: Names SQL injection, OS command injection, and path traversal, each with an ASVS reference and a Confidence rating.

tasks.intent: Review the source code in the current working directory for cryptography, secrets management, and configuration weaknesses. Produce the findings inline.
tasks.context_excerpt: Focus on crypto/config/secrets. The app is app.py.
tasks.reference: Names the hardcoded secret, weak MD5 password hashing, and debug mode enabled, each with severity, an ASVS reference, and a Confidence rating (High/Medium/Low).
